title: Live status: what a bank owes you when a hold turns into a case
intro: Holds stop fraud and meet the law. Revolut already handles the quick case well: a declined payment opens an in-app questionnaire, and confirming it unfreezes the card. In 4,391 recent App Store reviews, 61 describe a hold: 6 resolved fast and happily, 55 turned into cases that ran for days, and 23 of those complain about no timeline. This keeps the quick check and puts Revolut’s own 3-hour target on the screen for the long ones.

today.title: “Supporting documents”, nothing more
today.text: After the card is fixed, the hold gets a generic page: some features restricted, upload “supporting documents”, no timeline.

today.title: Every conversation starts again
today.text: Chat replies fast, but nobody can give a timeframe, and the next agent asks what the issue is. Built from reviews and help pages.

proposal.title: A calm status on Home
proposal.text: “£1,200 of this is on a short hold”, only Move carries a pause mark, and the card says everything else still works.

proposal.title: Exactly what’s needed
proposal.text: A statement showing this £1,200 on 9 Oct, and what it’s for. Each item is checked for glare and turns “Accepted” on arrival.

proposal.title: A live clock on its own promise
proposal.text: “2h 20m left of our 3-hour target”, from the moment everything arrived. What still works and what’s paused, as chips.

proposal.title: Delays announced early
proposal.text: If the target will slip, the app says why in plain terms, gives a new estimate, and says nothing is needed, before the first one passes.

lessons: Check what the product already does before proposing it. Revolut’s quick payment check exists and works; keep it.
People can accept not knowing why. They can’t accept not knowing when. Show the target you already have.
Ask for the exact item and confirm it on arrival. Vague requests make cases longer for everyone.
test: Does the live clock make people calmer, or add pressure? If 3 of 5 testers say it makes them more anxious, or a moved estimate costs more trust than no estimate, the idea needs rethinking.
note: Independent study by Mitul Vaghasiya, not affiliated with Revolut. Every screen below is my re-creation in Revolut’s visual style, based on its App Store screenshots (10 Oct 2026) and the public images listed in references/. They are not screenshots of the real app.

compare.title: Money on hold: before and after
compare.question: You’re abroad. A card payment is paused, then a £1,200 transfer from your other bank is held for review. Both versions keep Revolut’s real payment check and fast 24/7 chat. What changes is what you can see while the longer hold runs. Both phones are re-created in Revolut’s current visual style for an independent study.

before.try: Tap the push → Yes, it was me (Revolut’s real payment check). Then tap the restricted banner, upload, open Chat → Talk to a person, and press 3 hours later twice.
before.notice: The card check works well today. Then the hold: “supporting documents” with no specifics, no timeline, and a new agent who starts from zero.

after.try: Same card check. Then open the £1,200 card, send the 2 items, and press 3 hours later twice.
after.notice: Same card check. The hold shows exactly what’s needed, what still works, and a live clock against Revolut’s own 3-hour target. A delay is announced before the estimate passes.
